name: Paclitaxel
route_note: IV infusion with premedication (Cremophor-based); albumin-bound nab-paclitaxel needs no premedication
originator: US National Cancer Institute / Research Triangle Institute; developed by Bristol-Myers Squibb
owner: generic (many); Abraxane held by Bristol Myers Squibb

discovery.by: Monroe Wall and Mansukh Wani, Research Triangle Institute
discovery.note: Isolated from the bark of the Pacific yew (Taxus brevifolia) collected in a 1962 NCI plant-screening programme; structure published in 1971.

tagline: Pacific-yew taxane that freezes microtubules; mainstay for breast, ovarian and lung cancer
summary: Paclitaxel is a taxane diterpenoid that stabilises microtubules and arrests cells in mitosis. Originally extracted from Pacific yew bark and now produced by semisynthesis or plant-cell fermentation, it is a standard treatment for ovarian, breast, lung and many other cancers.
mechanism: Paclitaxel binds the β-tubulin subunit on the inner surface of microtubules, promoting assembly and preventing depolymerisation.

The resulting hyperstable, non-functional microtubules cannot form a normal mitotic spindle, so cells arrest at the G2/M transition and undergo apoptosis or mitotic catastrophe. Interference with microtubule transport in neurons underlies its peripheral neuropathy.
uses: Nab-paclitaxel: metastatic breast, NSCLC and pancreatic cancer (with gemcitabine)

history.title: Bark collected
history.detail: Botanist Arthur Barclay collects Pacific yew bark for the NCI screening programme.

history.title: Structure published
history.detail: Wall and Wani report the structure of taxol.

history.title: Mechanism
history.detail: Susan Horwitz shows that taxol stabilises microtubules, a novel mechanism.

history.title: Ovarian responses
history.detail: Johns Hopkins investigators report responses in refractory ovarian cancer; supply from bark becomes a major concern.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Taxol (Bristol-Myers Squibb) for refractory ovarian cancer; the name 'taxol' becomes a BMS trademark, so the generic name paclitaxel is adopted.

history.title: Semisynthesis
history.detail: Approval of semisynthetic paclitaxel from 10-deacetylbaccatin III (Holton route) from renewable yew needles.

history.title: Abraxane
history.detail: Albumin-bound nanoparticle paclitaxel approved for metastatic breast cancer.

history.title: Pancreatic cancer
history.detail: Nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine approved for metastatic pancreatic cancer (MPACT).

pk.half_life: about 3–52 hours depending on dose and infusion

safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning for anaphylaxis and severe hypersensitivity reactions (premedication required) and for bone-marrow suppression; do not give with baseline neutrophils below 1,500/mm³.

facts: Treating one patient originally required bark from several mature yew trees, driving the search for semisynthetic routes.
Total syntheses by Holton and by Nicolaou were both published in 1994.
